title: 8 arrested in deadly block party mass shooting, 2 on the run
text:
DOOLY COUNTY, Ga. (WALB/Gray News) - More people have been charged in connection with a deadly Georgia mass shooting that left two people dead and 44 injured.
In a press conference on Thursday, Nov. 5, law enforcement officials announced that eight people were charged following multiple searches across Crisp, Dooly and Houston counties.
Those arrested on Nov. 5. include:
- Latravis Keonta Bentley, 19, of Vienna, Ga.
- Ty’Darrious Ty’Jai Dawson, age 19, of Cordele, Ga.
- Devontre Jaquon Holton, age 23, of Cordele, Ga.
- Demari Jaheem Nixon, age 23, of Cordele, Ga.
- Kahdarious Kayvon Ray, age 17, of Vienna, Ga.
- Keontae Towns, age 16, of Cordele, Ga.
However, two additional suspects identified as 19-year-old Brexton Esamuel Gaston of Cordele and 34-year-old Vanravious Rashad Williams of Perry have warrants out for their arrests and are considered “armed and dangerous,” Peavy said.
Each is facing a number of serious charges including felony murder, aggravated assault, aggravated battery, participation of street gang activity, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony and Possession of a firearm under the age of 21, according to the GBI.
Ray was also previously arrested on Oct. 9 but now faces additional charges, while two others were arrested in the case on Oct. 14.
Investigators say that several guns were recovered during the searches on Thursday, and determined that several automatic weapons, including rifles and handguns, were used in the homecoming block party mass shooting on Oct. 4.
Authorities added that a total of 28 people were shot, including Ja’Quavion Aderious Jackson and Macaleb Malik Jackson, who died from their injuries, while 16 others were injured while fleeing the scene.
The GBI says the investigation remains ongoing and anyone with information is urged to contact its Perry office at 478-987-4545 or submit an anonymous tip at 1-800-597-8477.

title: Matt Dunlap concedes as 2nd District race heads to ranked-choice runoff
text:
Politics
Our political journalists are based in the Maine State House and have deep source networks across the partisan spectrum in communities all over the state. Their coverage aims to cut through major debates and probe how officials make decisions. Read more Politics coverage here.
Democrat Matt Dunlap on Thursday conceded to Republican Paul LePage even as the 2nd District race heads for a ranked-choice runoff.
In a statement, his campaign acknowledged the tough math, saying the runoff was unlikely to change the results.
“This isn’t the result we were hoping for, and I’m disappointed that we came short. Congratulations to Paul LePage, I wish him the best. I want to thank every volunteer who knocked doors, made calls, and made their voices heard. Your support inspired me, and I’m honored to have worked side by side with you over the past year,” Dunlap, the state auditor, said in a statement.
A ranked-choice tabulation will be held starting 10 a.m. Monday, the Maine secretary of state’s office said Thursday morning.
LePage’s 5,400-vote first-choice lead over Dunlap is more than double the edge that Democrat U.S. Rep. Jared Golden held when the Bangor Daily News and Decision Desk HQ called the 2nd District race in 2024. Golden won that runoff against Republican state Rep. Austin Theriault and a recount confirmed it.
To overtake LePage, Dunlap would need to net more than 5,418 votes from the 6,140 ballots that were blank or went to write-ins. But in the 2024 runoff, nearly 91% of ballots like those were set aside, and only 380 of more than 10,000 blanks moved to one of the candidates.
If 2024’s patterns hold, less than 300 blank ballots will transfer in the count. Even if Dunlap won all of them, he would still trail by more than 5,000 votes and would likely fall short of the 1.5-point margin needed for a state-funded recount.
LePage, a former governor, declared victory Wednesday afternoon at the Sea Dog in Bangor.
Brent Littlefield, a senior adviser to LePage, said in a Thursday statement that the former governor has an “extremely large” lead over Dunlap heading into a ranked-choice runoff.
“Paul LePage looks forward to working for all of the people of Maine’s 2nd District, working with anyone – and everyone – regardless of Party to put Maine first,” Littlefield said.
Maine Republican Party Chair Jim Deyermond congratulated LePage on his win Thursday afternoon, saying the party is “grateful” for his return to public office.
“Gov. LePage brought common sense back to the Blaine House, and now he is bringing it to Washington, D.C., on behalf of Congressional District 2. Paul LePage always puts people before politics, without fail,” Deyermond said.
Republican National Committee spokesperson Kristen Cianci praised LePage for flipping the 2nd District, echoing Deyermond by saying that the former governor will bring “common sense” to Washington and “deliver for Mainers.”
BDN writer Michael Shepherd contributed to this report.

title: Pavel Zacha lifts Bruins to win over Penguins
text:
PITTSBURGH — Pavel Zacha scored twice and the Boston Bruins beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night.
Morgan Geekie scored in his third straight game and had an assist. Elias Lindholm, Mark Kastelic and Fraser Minten also scored for the Bruins, who have won three straight. Boston has won 10 of its last 13 games overall.
David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka added two assists and Michael DiPietro stopped 16 shots for the Bruins, who snapped a three-game road losing streak. Boston has points in its last seven trips to Pittsburgh, dating to Nov. 1, 2022.
Justin Brazeau scored his first goal in his second game of the season since returning from a training camp injury. Nick Robertson also scored for the Penguins, who struggled defensively against the Bruins.
Pittsburgh captain Sidney Crosby did not record a point and remains tied with Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time scoring list with 1,771 points.
Arturs Silovs made 18 saves for the Penguins, who lost their fourth straight. Pittsburgh has dropped eight of its last 10 games overall.
Boston led 3-1 after the first period and 5-2 through 40 minutes.
Zacha scored both of his goals on a 2-on-1, as did Minten. Geekie scored on a partial breakaway after a poor Pittsburgh line change, and Lindholm found the back of the net following an Erik Karlsson turnover in his own zone. Karlsson was a minus-4 for Pittsburgh.
Up next
Bruins: Open a four-game homestand Sunday against Florida. Boston plays 10 of its next 11 games at home.
Penguins: Begin a three-game West Coast trip Saturday at Los Angeles.

title: Democrat upsets a lightning-rod western Maine sheriff by 68 votes
text:
Oxford County Sheriff Christopher Wainwright, a Republican whom Gov. Janet Mills declined to remove from office two years ago, lost his bid for re-election by 68 votes in Tuesday’s election.
A recount is likely in the race that looks set to usher in Democrat Timothy Holland, a school resource officer and 45-year police veteran, as sheriff. He won 33.9% of votes to 33.7% for Wainwright and 29.5% for independent Justin Brown, who is among three deputies making a civil rights complaint against Wainwright alleging illegal retaliation.
Neither Holland nor Wainwright could be reached on Thursday after the secretary of state’s office reported the result to Bangor Daily News. The day began with the race appearing to go the other way. Holland posted on Facebook in the morning that he trailed Wainwright by 12 votes by the candidates’ own count, saying he would ask for a recount.
But Holland won despite the three-way split that both challengers had worried would hand Wainwright a third term. The race was voters’ first chance to weigh in on Wainwright since 2024, when he survived Maine’s most serious attempt to remove a sheriff in nearly a century.
In 2022, Wainwright pressured a deputy to dismiss a traffic ticket for a woman he had grown up with, then berated the deputies who reported it in a recorded phone call. The next year, the BDN found he had sent uncertified officers into schools and traded guns from evidence to a gun shop for credit with almost no paperwork.
A county investigator concluded Wainwright may have committed theft, though he was never charged. The all-Republican county commission unanimously asked Mills to remove him in February 2024. She called his conduct unprofessional but said it didn’t meet the constitutional standard for removal, saying voters should decide his fate.
Wainwright, of Dixfield, joined the sheriff’s office at 19 and has spent 36 years there. He rose to the top after his role in an FBI investigation into then-Sheriff Wayne Gallant, who was accused of sexually harassing several people and resigned in 2017. Wainwright won the open seat the next year.
He and Brown criticized each other frequently during the campaign, with Wainwright accusing his deputy of running a negative race and pointing to Brown’s role in a police shooting. But the sheriff and Holland were friendlier, with Wainwright saying early Thursday that he respected his Democratic opponent.
Conservative Oxford County was a bright spot for Democrats in this year’s election. In the closest election of its kind, Beth Bosworth of Fryeburg won an open seat over former Rep. John Andrews, R-Paris. Party candidates also flipped three House seats based in Norway, Fryeburg and Bridgton.
Daniel O’Connor is a Report for America corps member who covers rural government as part of the partnership between the Bangor Daily News and The Maine Monitor, with additional support from BDN and Monitor readers.

title: To the Batpod!: Batman’s motorbike could fetch 1.2 million at movie memorabilia auction
text:
To the Batpod!: Batman’s motorbike could fetch 1.2 million at movie memorabilia auction
Batman’s motorbike, known as the Batpod, is going under the hammer as part of a movie memorabilia auction, with an estimate of up to £900,000 ($1.2 million).
The vehicle was used in Christopher Nolan movies “The Dark Knight” (2008) and “The Dark Knight Rises” (2012), both of which starred Christian Bale as Batman, and is being sold by auction house Propstore Auction.
“It’s a cracking thing,” Stephen Lane, CEO and founder of Propstore, told CNN on Thursday.
Lane said that the vehicle, which is known as “The Beast,” was designed by Nolan himself in conjunction with production designer Nathan Crowley. Chris Korvold, an Academy Award winner for visual effects, was then tasked with bringing it to life.
Related video above: Nostalgia sparks new movie store opening in South Philadelphia
“It’s actually quite a feat of engineering … to actually have that thing practically working on set,” said Lane, explaining that the bike uses a 750cc Honda engine and “monstrous” 31-inch tires.
“I know that it was a really, really tricky thing for the actors to sit on, but also the stunt guys to actually drive this practically as well,” he added.
Lane said there were a number of incidents in which someone lost control of the Batpod, including one that was captured on video in which the vehicle “smashes into one of the cameras.”
“It basically sort of careers out of control and knocks the camera over,” he said. “So, I think it was a very, very tricky thing.”
The bike is one of six made, but it’s the only one that has been officially released by Warner Bros. Studios, said Lane.
“Vehicles like this are just so desirable because of their unique nature and because of their impressive aesthetic as well,” he said.
“It’s got to be one of the most impressive looking and … memorable, I would say, movie vehicles of all time,” he added.
Online bidding opened on Thursday and will close on Dec. 4 at a live auction in London.
The Batpod is being sold alongside hundreds of other pieces of movie memorabilia, including two complete Batsuits – one worn by Bale in 2005’s “Batman Begins” and another worn 10 years earlier by Val Kilmer in “Batman Forever.”
Other items going under the hammer include the fedora and shirt worn by stuntman Vic Armstrong in “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom” (1984) and “Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade” (1989), as well as the sword used by Kit Harington’s Jon Snow in the “Game of Thrones” television series.
Also among the movie memorabilia is Freddy Krueger’s glove, which met its reserve price of £25,000 ($34,000) just a few hours after the auction went live.
More than 100 lots will go on display at a preview exhibition at the Cumberland Hotel in London from Nov. 19 to Nov. 22.

title: First Trump administration senior official resigns post-midterms
text:
Harmeet Dhillon, who runs the Justice Department’s Civil Rights division, resigns
Harmeet Dhillon has resigned from her post as the head of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, making her the first senior official to leave the administration since the midterms.
Attorney General Todd Blanche announced her resignation in a social media post, saying that she has “led the Civil Rights Division with conviction.”
“She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor,” Blanche wrote on X “The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors.”
In her year and a half as Assistant Attorney General, Dhillon upended the division in an attempt to reshape its work to fit into the Trump era — shifting from its traditional work enforcing laws encouraging elections access and police reform to fighting what she has called “woke ideology.”
In recent weeks, Dhillon, a former legal adviser to President Donald Trump’s campaign, appeared increasingly sidelined as the department pursued a series of high-profile election-related legal cases of high interest to the president.
“Where’s Harmeet?” asked one GOP official working on some of the legal cases the department pursued to try to support Trump’s claims of Democrats trying to steal the election.
Dhillon took on a high profile albeit non-traditional presence on social media, announcing initiatives alongside her love of knitting, while embracing right-wing causes, including opening a section dedicated to the Second Amendment and promoting gun ownership.
She leaves behind a division faltering due to a lack of staffing — more than 75% of the Civil Rights Division was fired or quit during her term. She recruited several conservative lawyers to join the division in their place, but those hires have far from made up for the ouster of decades of knowledge on civil rights laws.
In fact, the gutting of the Civil Rights Division was part of the problem for Dhillon because some conservatives complained that inexperienced lawyers in her section weren’t able to handle cases referred to her division.
Dhillon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Dhillon’s departure was all but guaranteed to come in the days following the election. Her control over the Civil Rights Division had been declining for months, officials familiar with the matter said, in part because of her repeated losses in court and the perception among colleagues that she was good at announcing initiatives and less effective at accomplishing them.
The largest losses Dhillon suffered in court were over her attempts to gain access to voter rolls. Judges across the country tossed lawsuits that Dhillon claimed would help states “clean” their rolls of non-citizens, sharply criticizing what they saw as an effort to use the law to disenfranchise voters or access their personal data.
Dhillon was increasingly sidelined from the department’s voting efforts as the midterms approached, sources told CNN. As the election approached, it was Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter who signed on to the highest profile lawsuits, not Dhillon.
Stanley Woodward, Associate Attorney General, with whom Dhillon had a strained relationship, took the lead appearing in court defending the administration’s legal moves.
Still, other efforts she spearheaded came with mixed success. She sent letters to and filed lawsuits against universities she accused of brad antisemitism and discrimination largely against white students, for example, gut those efforts rarely resulted in a court win — or even in a lawsuit at all.
Some of the universities committed to help root out antisemitism, but sources have told CNN there was little framework or follow up from the department at all.

title: Biddeford harbormaster placed on leave amid pier controversy
text:
Biddeford Harbormaster Paul Lariviere has been placed on paid administrative leave, interim City Manager Cornell Knight confirmed Thursday.
Knight declined say why Lariviere was put on leave or to comment further, describing it as a personnel matter. He told the Biddeford Gazette, which first reported the news, that Assistant Harbormaster Randy Desmaris will likely be appointed to fill Lariviere’s role permanently.
Neither Lariviere or Desmaris responded to requests for comment Thursday afternoon.
The Biddeford City Council met Thursday evening, though Lariviere’s situation was not discussed. The council did confirm Laurie Smith as the new city manager, replacing Knight.
CONFLICTS OVER BIAS, ROLE
Over the past few years, Lariviere and city leaders have clashed over the controversial University of New England pier proposal on the Saco River.
Lariviere has not been allowed to participate in or advise on the project since 2024, after he made several public comments in opposition to the project. Then-City Manager James Bennett said those remarks “tarnished” the presumption that UNE’s application would be considered objectively.
Bennett also said Lariviere “spent time lobbying the Harbor Commission and agencies to tell people why they should back his decision” about the best location for the pier. Lariviere showed bias against the project before it was even brought to the city planning board, Bennett added.
Lariviere has maintained that he will not approve the pier or relocate moorings to allow for its construction. Under city code, the harbormaster is required to sign off on waterway projects like this before a building permit can be issued.
But the city attorney has contended that, based on his interpretation of the code, the harbormaster’s approval is moot. The harbormaster is simply a facilitator in projects like this, Harry Center said last week, so his view is that Lariviere’s approval is unnecessary for the project to proceed.
The Saco River Corridor Commission, the City Council and the planning board have all given UNE the go-ahead for the project, Center noted.
Kyle Noble, a Hills Beach resident who has been outspoken about the pier project, said Thursday that he believes the city should replace Center with someone “familiar with Maine’s maritime law.”
“Otherwise we will continue to be pushed around by a public relations department and legal staff,” he said. “At least (Lariviere) and I, and others, will be able to say, ‘I told you so.’”
A CONTROVERSIAL PROJECT
The research pier would be located along the Saco River near the Arthur P. Girard Marine Science Center on UNE’s Biddeford campus. The school has said it would allow students and professors to conduct waterfront research year-round, which both students and staff have said would be beneficial.
Since its proposal in 2024, the pier has faced backlash from some residents, many of whom worry about the number of moorings that would need to be moved and a 250-foot vegetative buffer zone that was not taken into consideration prior to the proposal.
Biddeford and UNE spent months sparring over the project in legal filings, during public meetings and through statements to the press.
But in August, the Saco River Corridor Commission granted the university a 2-year extension for construction, and soon after, the city dropped an appeal to have Maine’s highest court stop the project. Mayor Liam LaFountain said at the time that the commission’s extension had made such an appeal pointless, because if the court had ordered another review of the matter, the SRCC would simply have upheld its own decision.
In October, the City Council lifted an ongoing moratorium on UNE development, and a day later, the planning board voted to extend the university’s permit for the project. The city and UNE then issued a joint statement suggesting that they were mending their strained ties.
Soon after, UNE began clearing some trees to create an access road to the pier’s planned location.
Editor’s note: This story was updated on Nov. 6 to include information from Thursday night’s City Council meeting.

title: Bridgton‑Lake Region Rotary Club partners with CrossWalk Community Outreach for Veterans Day lunch
text:
NAPLES — The Bridgton‑Lake Region Rotary Club will partner with CrossWalk Community Outreach to host a Veterans Day luncheon from 1 to 3 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 11 at CrossWalk’s new facility, 11 October Road in Naples. The meal will follow the noon color guard presentation at the Naples monument. The luncheon honors veterans and their guests from throughout the area, all of whom are invited to enjoy chili dogs or chicken sliders free of charge. Please RSVP at www.crosswalkco.org.
New Rotarian Charlotte Kelly is championing the event.
“Charlotte has brought a whole new level of veterans activities to the club,” Rotary Club President Rick Whelchel said. “In addition to this luncheon, we helped fund two guardians on a recent Maine Honor Flight and will soon host the new director and the two guardians at an upcoming meeting. Charlotte is a real asset to the club.”
Kelly added, “I’m passionate about serving veterans. I’ve been a Maine Honor Flight Guardian, am a member of the American Legion Auxiliary Post 155 and stay active with other local veterans organizations.”
CrossWalk Community Outreach will host the luncheon from its new full‑service facility, which provides essential support for individuals facing mental health challenges, addiction recovery, domestic abuse, homelessness or difficulties navigating public benefits. title: Tips to reduce utility costs around the house
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Between the grocery checkout and the gas pump, there’s no shortage of reminders that everyday life is expensive.
Keeping the lights on, the water hot and the house warm adds another layer to the household budget, especially here in Maine. According to the Maine Department of Energy Resources, we use more residential heating oil per person than any other state, and about half of our households rely on it as their primary heating source. As temperatures drop, finding ways to save becomes even more essential.
We can’t control utility rates, but a few simple changes around the house may help keep monthly bills in check. You don’t have to tackle every change at once. Start with a few bulbs, check the air filter and take a look at what’s plugged in. These small adjustments can help you get a better handle on what your household uses and what you pay each month.
Reconsider your existing lighting.
Replacing older bulbs with LEDs is a simple way to use less electricity without giving up a bright room. According to energy provider Reliant, a traditional incandescent bulb uses about 60 watts, while an LED bulb needs just 8 to 12 watts to produce the same amount of light. Many households have already made the change, but check the fixtures you use less often, too.
Identify and address devices consuming energy when not in use.
Some electronics keep drawing power even when they appear to be off. These so-called energy vampires include certain kitchen appliances, DVRs and computers. Fortunately, saving electricity doesn’t have to mean making the rounds to unplug everything before bed. Advanced power strips can automatically cut power to connected accessories when a primary device, such as a television, is turned off. Check how the strip works and which devices should stay powered before plugging everything in.
Adjust your water heater temperature.
A hot shower is one of life’s small pleasures, but keeping water hotter than necessary can add to your bills. The U.S. Department of Energy says water heating accounts for about 18% of a home’s utility costs. Some manufacturers set water heaters at 140 degrees, although 120 degrees is sufficient for many households. Lowering the setting may reduce the energy used to heat water. Check the manufacturer’s guidance and your household’s needs before making an adjustment.
Pay attention to HVAC filters.
Air filters are easy to forget until you pull one out and see what it has collected. A dirty filter restricts airflow, making your heating and cooling system work harder to circulate air. That extra effort uses more energy and can drive up your bill. Carrier recommends changing filters every 30 to 90 days. Set a reminder to check yours regularly, and follow the recommendations for your system and filter.

title: California Gov. Gavin Newsom says he will commute all 548 death sentences in state to life without parole
text:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — California Gov. Gavin Newsom said Thursday that he’ll change all death sentences in the state to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
There are 548 people on death row in California.
Newsom’s decision comes as he prepares to leave office after eight years. In 2019, he placed a moratorium on executions in the state but hundreds of people remained on death row.
“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” Newsom said in a letter.
According to the state constitution, the California Supreme Court’s approval is required to grant clemency to anyone convicted of a felony more than once.
Newsom said the decision was among the most difficult choices of his career because it will surface painful memories for crime victims’ families.
“As Governor, I alone bear responsibility for this decision and its impact, just as I alone would bear responsibility for each execution,” Newsom wrote.

title: Milford man stopped bringing children to doctors before toddler froze to death, court doc says
text:
The man accused of letting his toddler freeze to death had been negligent with his children in the weeks before, according to a probable cause affidavit.
Shane McLaughlin, 37, didn’t bring his three children to multiple medical appointments in December 2025 while there was an active investigation by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services, a 35-page report from Maine State Police said.
McLaughlin, of Milford, is charged with one felony count of manslaughter, as well as three counts of child endangerment, in Penobscot County Superior Court. His 1-year-old daughter, Eleanora Ray McLaughlin, died of hypothermia at the family’s home on Dec. 28.
His attorney and DHHS did not respond to requests for comment.
McLaughlin’s now-3-year-old son woke up asking for a drink around 4:30 a.m. and the father discovered Eleanora was dead in her playpen, the report said.
Her twin sister was hypothermic when EMS arrived, but a warm, dry blanket helped get her body temperature up to normal by the time she arrived at the hospital, the report said. Her older brother was fine.
“One can opine” that the twin sister may have suffered a similar fate to Eleanora if McLaughlin hadn’t gotten up to get his son a drink, the police affidavit said.
There was no heat in the Milford home the night of Eleanora’s death. McLaughlin had been using a space heater for the bedroom where he and the children slept. Each twin slept in their own playpen, with the space heater between them.
McLaughlin said he could see his breath when he woke up that day, the report said. It was 18 degrees in the home when police arrived and -10 degrees outside.
During an interview with police, McLaughlin was shocked to learn Eleanora died of hypothermia and said he didn’t understand how it could have happened, the report said.
The details in the document come from the Maine State Police investigation and interviews with DHHS case workers. McLaughlin and his ex-wife, Erika, had their parental rights terminated for another child in 2018, the report said. She left Maine the summer before Eleanora’s death and had limited contact with her children.
McLaughlin was negligent in providing a safe environment for his children, the report said. His mother lived just over a mile down the road and had adequate heat, but he did not ask if they could stay there. He also didn’t ask his former mother-in-law, who lives in Bangor.
He told police he hated asking for help because people either ask for help in return or run their mouth, the report said. He “negligently put his pride ahead of the safety of his children,” the report said.
Two investigations in 2025 were closed by DHHS with no findings of neglect by McLaughlin. The second investigation was closed six days before Eleanora’s death. While the investigation was open, McLaughlin failed to bring the kids to three doctor’s appointments.
One concern for the appointments included cellulitis on Eleanora’s foot. A medical professional previously tried to explain the seriousness of the infection, but McLaughlin didn’t seem to grasp the situation, the report said.
When first responders arrived at the home, they found the kitchen littered with trash and feces, with unwashed dishes and food everywhere, the report said. The room smelled like urine, feces and smoke. There was no running water in the home.
However, when DHHS made a prescheduled home visit in November, the case worker found no safety concerns, the report said. The worker did not check to see if there was running water in the home.
There were concerns within DHHS but there wasn’t enough evidence to keep a case open, the report said. A July 2025 case also found no safety concerns.
McLaughlin would not accept recommendations from medical professionals for child development specialists because he felt targeted, the report said.
A Jan. 22 report from DHHS substantiated findings of child abuse and neglect by McLaughlin. The two surviving children were taken from his custody and placed with their maternal grandmother.
Before his arrest last week, McLaughlin had been working toward reunification through DHHS. The department said it’s too soon to say what will happen next in that case.
McLaughlin is held in the Penobscot County Jail on a $250,000 cash bail.

title: Warm Friday With Rain Spreading South To North Late In The Day
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Cloud cover will hold firm overnight with a few light showers in the north and areas of drizzle elsewhere. Lows will be on the warmer side, ranging from the upper 40s to the upper 50s. Watch for areas of patchy fog developing overnight.
Friday: Last Mild Day, Rain Arrives Late
A cold front will stall along the Maine coast early Friday morning, guiding in broken showers for coastal communities before clearing shortly after sunrise.
Expect mostly cloudy to overcast skies through the day, with the greatest opportunity for glimpses of sunshine found the farther north you live. Friday will also bring one final mild day, with afternoon highs climbing into the 60s.
Our next weather-maker arrives by late Friday afternoon. An area of low pressure will ride northeast along the stalled front, spreading rainfall into the coastline first before working inland through Friday night.
Weekend Outlook: Showers & Cooling Down
The coastal low will pass through the Gulf of Maine Friday night into early Saturday. The exact track of the system will dictate how far inland steady rain pushes, but plan on wet conditions to start Saturday morning. Rain will transition to lighter, more scattered showers through Saturday afternoon, a few spots may even see the rain ending for a period of time. Highs will be in the low to mid-50s.
Scattered showers linger into Sunday as the system slowly pulls away. Temperatures drop further, with highs only reaching the 40s. A few higher elevations could see snowflakes mix in before precipitation comes to an end.
Projected Rainfall Totals:
- Immediate Coast: 1-2+ inches
- Interstate to Coast: 1 to 2 inches
- Foothills to Interstate: 0.5 to 1 inch
- Mountains and Northern Maine: Less than 0.5 inches
Rainfall amounts remain sensitive to the track of the low. A track farther north would increase totals, while a shift south would trim amounts back.
Drier and more seasonable weather returns to start the new workweek.
First Alert 7-Day Forecast
TONIGHT: Showers ending early. Cloudy skies with patchy fog. Lows ranging from the upper 40s to the upper 50s. SW wind 5-15 mph.
FRIDAY: Mostly cloudy to overcast skies with rain arriving later in the day along the coast and spreads inland overnight. Highs in the 60s. NW wind 5-10 mph.
SATURDAY: Cloudy with rain possible. Light showers by the afternoon. Highs in the low to mid 50s. NE wind 10-20 mph.
SUNDAY: Mostly cloudy with scattered showers possible. Highs in the 40s.
MONDAY: Partly to mostly cloudy skies. Highs in the 40s and low 50s.
TUESDAY: Partly to mostly cloudy skies. Highs in the 40s and low 50s.

title: Hegseth allows National Guard to boost DC patrols with military vehicles, boats and patrol cars
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has signed off on the National Guard ramping up its presence in the nation’s capital in military vehicles and boats as troops deepen their integration with local law enforcement.
In two memos signed Oct. 29 and obtained by The Associated Press, Hegseth approved the National Guard to use 60 military police cars as well as tactical vehicles, patrol boats and portable light towers during increased patrols around Washington. Troops will also be able to carry rifles during some operations but not in Metro rail stations.
The sight of vehicles that look more at home on a battlefield than a city street will harken back to when President Donald Trump first deployed the National Guard in August 2025 for what he called a crime-fighting mission. Tactical vehicles and troops carrying guns initially were seen at some Washington landmarks. National Guard members have supported law enforcement operations, patrolled neighborhoods, dispersed homeless camps and helped with citywide cleanup efforts.
A boost in troop presence comes amid increased issues involving Guard members assigned to the city, including the arrest of a Georgia serviceman for pulling a gun on a fellow Guard member, the arrest of a Guard member for carrying an unauthorized firearm, and the shooting of a Guardsman while trying to break up a fight.
The memos say “visibility patrols,” a mainstay of the Guard’s mission in Washington, are going to be expanded and 20 light towers will be employed to “enhance force protection in patrol zones.”
But Hegseth says the maximum number of deployed Guard members would stay at 3,500, lower than a summertime peak of about 5,000 during America’s 250th anniversary celebrations.
Hegseth signed off on the National Guard using patrol cars and tactical vehicles to support law enforcement operations, though the memos stressed that the patrol cars need to be marked as “National Guard” and troops need to be in uniform. Two National Guard patrol boats will also be used “to provide operational maritime support.” The memos forbid troops from conducting high-speed chases.
The memos suggest that troops will play a greater role in taking on “gangs and drug traffickers.” Hegseth is continuing to provide six analysts “to address organized drug distribution within D.C.,” and troops who are supporting anti-gang and drug operations will now be able to carry rifles in addition to their traditional pistols.
One of the memos grants the U.S. Marshals Service the use of the D.C. National Guard’s 260th Special Purpose Brigade — a unit that functioned as a “quick reaction force” — to help protect “key federal leaders” and help secure and defend “key federal facilities.”
A Marshals Service request for National Guard helicopters or the use of troops “to clean up abandoned tires in specific areas of D.C.” was denied in a Nov. 4 memo, however.
When asked about the memos, the Pentagon confirmed that Hegseth “authorized the continued use of National Guard personnel and capabilities in support of the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful mission.”
The District of Columbia, which sued in September 2025 over the National Guard deployment, has argued that the mobilization is an illegal use of the military for domestic law enforcement. A federal appeals court panel heard arguments Oct. 14 after a lower court sided with the city.
Nearly 3,100 Guard members from various states are in Washington, including more than 500 from Georgia, the largest contingent behind the District of Columbia, which had 514 members involved as of Monday.

title: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault by London jury
text:
Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault by London jury
Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault charges on allegations dating back more than 20 years.
Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand would receive a prison term when he is sentenced Monday. He was taken into custody.
A prosecutor said the British actor-comedian was a ruthless, calculating, manipulative “sexual predator.”
Brand, 51, denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man and once led a promiscuous life but had never forced anyone to do something against their will.
Brand was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.
The jury of eight men and four women in Southwark Crown Court deliberated more than eight hours over two days.
Known for risqué stand-up routines and battles with drugs and alcohol, Brand rose to prominence in the early 2000s, hosting television programs and his own BBC radio show. He appeared in Hollywood films including “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” and “Get Him to the Greek” and was briefly married to pop star Katy Perry.
In recent years he has moved away from mainstream media, relocated to Florida and built a large online following with videos mixing wellness, conspiracy theories and discussions of his religious devotion.
Brand said the criminal case had a devastating impact on his life and family.
“My entire life has been consumed by these events, these allegations, these accusations,” he said.
Brand’s lawyers argued that the alleged victims were undermined by the fact that they only went to police years after the alleged assaults, and following the broadcast of a 2023 documentary that contained anonymous allegations against Brand.
Brand testified that friends and colleagues had abandoned him.
His wife, Laura, who accompanied him to court, testified as a character witness in his defense, but no one with relevant evidence was willing to give evidence on his behalf, Brand said.

title: Referendum vote for potential jail outside Bangor too close to call

BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - There is still a razor-thin margin Wednesday night in Penobscot County, where voters are still waiting on the final outcome of Question One.
The referendum asks whether county commissioners can search outside of Bangor for a new potential jail site.
Right now, “yes” leads by just 149 votes—holding roughly 50-point-one percent to 49-point-nine percent.
Results from 10 municipalities are still outstanding.
County officials say towns have three days to submit their totals, but they hope to have a clearer picture by tomorrow or Friday.
Question One only authorizes a site search—any future plans to actually build a new jail would require another vote.

title: Teen missing for over a year found at home of man who sexually assaulted her, removed braces with pliers, police say
text:
HUNTINGTON, Ore. (AP) — A 17-year-old girl from Utah who went missing in May 2025 was found at the home of an Oregon man who’s been charged with transporting her across state lines with the intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.
Authorities acting on a tip rescued the girl Sunday at a home in Huntington, Oregon, and arrested Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, in a traffic stop about 30 miles away.
The missing girl told another child she met online that she had run away and was being held against her will at a man’s house in Oregon.
On Sunday, a parent of the other child contacted the missing Utah girl by video — and the FBI listened in.
During the call, the missing girl said that she met Harmel on social media and that he had driven her from Utah to Oregon, an FBI agent said in court records.
She also said Harmel threw her phone in a river; told her she couldn’t leave his home; made her sleep against a wall to prevent her from escaping from the bed they shared; often hit her; sexually assaulted her; and forced her to remove her braces with pliers so she couldn’t be identified, according to the FBI.
No lawyer for Harmel was listed in court records.
The federal public defender’s office in Utah declined to comment when The Associated Press asked if it represented Harmel. The AP also reached out through social media to someone believed to be related to Harmel.

title: ‘Criminal’ Comic Series Comes to Streaming in First Trailer
text:
‘Criminal,’ Hit Comic Book, Becomes Streaming Series in First Trailer
For the last 20 years, one of the best and longest-running comic series has been Criminal by writer Ed Brubaker and artist Sean Phillips. The book is an anthology of crime stories all set within the same world, but focused on different characters.
Now the show is becoming a TV series for Amazon’s Prime Video service, with Brubaker and Phillips both involved as executive producers. (You may not know Brubaker by name but as the co-creator of the Winter Soldier character, you probably know his work.)
Criminal’s first season adapts the comic’s first volume which consisted of two separate storylines: “Coward” and “Lawless.” Prime is actually releasing them that way too; as two batches of episodes released several weeks apart.
The trailer for the series, though, features footage from both parts, and shows off stars Charlie Hunnam, Adria Arjona, Emilia Clarke, and Luke Evans, who looks really mean and nasty, like a Sean Phillips illustration come to life.
READ MORE: The Worst Adaptations of Great Comic Books
Here is the series’ official synopsis from Amazon:
Criminal begins with the story of two friends, Leo Patterson (Charlie Hunnam) and Ricky Lawless (Gus Halper), one trying to fight his way out of the world of crime they were raised in, the other desperate to follow in the footsteps of his father, a legendary outlaw. And when Ricky's older brother Tracy (Luke Evans) returns home from the Army, their tragic family history comes home with him. Drawn into their orbit are Greta (Adria Arjona), a sharp-tongued car thief from Leo’s past, and Mallory (Emilia Clarke), Ricky's girlfriend, who fears what he'll do to get by. Gunfights, heists, and tragic romance are the order of the day, but will anyone make it out alive?
Criminal debuts on Prime Video on January 13 with its adaptation of “Coward.” Then Part 2, with the TV version of “Lawless” follows on January 27. Each part consists of four episodes.

title: 1 deputy dies and another not expected to survive after firefight with suspect at Washington home
text:
SPOKANE, Wash. (AP) — One of two sheriff’s deputies wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Washington state has died, and the other is not expected to survive, authorities said Wednesday.
Deputies responded to a home in Spangle, a small farming community south of Spokane, on Tuesday afternoon after a woman told her neighbor that she had been shot by her brother, the Spokane County Sheriff’s Office said.
They determined the suspect had a felony warrant and that there might be other victims, and SWAT team members and deputies tried to breach the door.
Gunfire erupted from the home, and the two deputies were struck. They were taken to a hospital in critical condition. One died that night, and the other was being kept on life support Wednesday, allowing for the donation of his organs, the sheriff’s office said in a written statement.
“He will continue to serve others with the gift of life,” the statement said.
Neither was identified, but Sheriff John Nowels described them as younger members of the SWAT team. The deputy who died had a wife and two children.
“Although we know our Deputies knew the risks, they bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know,” the sheriff’s office said. “They did this with honor and with an unwavering sense of duty.”
Other deputies returned fire and found the suspect dead inside, along with one other victim in the house and one in the yard, authorities said.
The names of the victims and the suspect have not been released.
Authorities are investigating the shooting and what may have led to it.
The woman who reported being shot by her brother was hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries.

title: Undeveloped 30-acre island in Blue Hill Bay hits the market for $1.75M
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Housing
This section of the BDN aims to help readers understand Maine’s housing crisis, the volatile real estate market and the public policy behind them. Read more Housing coverage here.
A 30-acre private island located just north of Swans Island in Blue Hill Bay is on the market for the first time in at least 50 years.
Orono Island, part of the Acadia Archipelago, is largely undeveloped except for two docks and a roughly 10-by-20-foot shelter with wooden sleeping bunks, according to Story Litchfield of LandVest Inc., the listing agent for the property.
The property hit the market on Monday with an asking price of more than $1.7 million and has already garnered the attention of multiple prospective buyers, Litchfield said.
“It’s very rare for an entire island to become available,” Litchfield said. “Sometimes islands are much more remote. This is independent of Swans Island and Bass Harbor, but still very accessible.”
The island was once owned by Margaret “Peggy” Rockefeller, according to the state’s Coastal Island Registry.
The wooded island is a 20-minute boat ride from Bass Harbor and offers paths, picnic spots and sandy beaches. One of the island’s piers is a granite wharf that functions as a deepwater dock while the other is a tidal dock.
A conservation easement on the island restricts development to one residential building and necessary outbuildings, Litchfield said. The island cannot host any commercial properties or more than one home.
There’s no running water, septic system or electricity on the property, making it entirely off-grid. One well has been dug, but the fresh water hasn’t been used for drinking, according to Litchfield.
With a high point of roughly 62 feet, the island offers 360-degree scenic views of boating traffic on Casco Passage and the neighboring islands.
The sellers have a home on Mount Desert Island and for decades used Orono Island as a place for picnics and family gatherings.
“They feel it’s time for the family to pass it along for someone else to enjoy,” Litchfield said.
The island would be ideal for anyone fond of boating, hiking and “anyone with an interest in Maine’s coastal island environments,” Litchfield said. The sellers would also love the next owner to be similarly “conservation-minded.”

title: Elon Musk spent at least $445 million to boost Republicans in the midterms
text:
AUSTIN, Texas (AP) — Elon Musk spent at least $445 million in a gambit to help Republicans keep control of Congress, an amount roughly equivalent to someone on a $100,000 annual salary saving every penny for 4,400 years.
To the world’s first trillionaire, it’s a pittance, but the billions of dollars’ worth of business his companies do with the federal government is not. And on Tuesday night, a Republican Party that had embraced Musk lost again and again, ceding control of Congress to a Democratic Party leery of the world’s richest person and keen to put his companies and his work at the Department of Government Efficiency under a microscope.
Nobody may have suffered bigger losses Tuesday than President Donald Trump. But few others had more on the line than Musk, who gambled big and came up holding the midterm’s worst return on investment. Democrats in Congress were already queuing to get their shot at Musk, with possible subpoenas and investigations.
As the bloodiest election for Republicans in recent history wore on, Musk joked on X, the social media site he owns. “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” he wrote with a shrug emoji.
Musk now faces new threats to his bottom line in places including Texas, where he has based himself and several of his companies. Musk spent at least $5 million to try to reelect Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who lost. Democrats also secured control of the Texas House and the U.S. Senate, partly by beating Texas Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, who effectively benefited from $158 million of Musk’s spending but lost his Senate race against Democrat James Talarico.
It was the first statewide win for Democrats in Texas in more than 30 years, and the candidates won in part by hammering Musk, the tax breaks and grants his companies receive, and his relationships with elected Republicans.
“This era of open corruption is going to come to an end,” said Rep. Gene Wu, chairman of the state legislature’s newly empowered Democratic Caucus.
Musk did not respond to messages seeking comment.
Musk’s reputation did not help with many Texas voters
Slightly more than half of Texas voters said they had an unfavorable opinion of Musk, according to The AP Voter Poll of more than 5,000 voters in the state. While Musk is overwhelmingly viewed positively by MAGA Republicans, those numbers dip for non-MAGA GOP voters and plummet for independent and Democratic voters.
Those were the voters who Talarico and Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who beat Abbott in the governor’s race, were targeting. The two often framed politics not through partisanship but as billionaires versus everyday Texans, and Musk’s emergence as a major Republican benefactor played into that message.
“Paxton is funded by one dude. Elon Musk wants our land. He wants our water. He wants our tax dollars. He wants his very own personal United States senator,” Talarico told a crowd in his final rally of the election, just after Hinojosa gave a similar excoriation on the same Austin stage.
“We know that Elon Musk got a $1.7 billion property tax break here in Texas, property taxes that the rest of us have to pay full price on,” Hinojosa said.
Even as Musk’s money helped blanket Texas in negative ads largely against Talarico, the Democrats’ message was aimed at the heart of an electorate whose median household income of $85,000 a year is under a pressure test as the prices of gas, groceries, rents and mortgages keep climbing.
Outgoing Rep. Chip Roy, R-Texas, said there was a point where the sheer amount of Musk’s donations became unhelpful to the GOP’s effort.
“You’re reaching the upper bound of the benefit of any of these dollars,” he said in an interview. “People are so turned off by all of the ads, and all you’re doing is running the same ad every single time.”
Investor jitters after election drop Musk’s net worth by $45 billion
Musk’s two publicly traded companies, Tesla and SpaceX, both saw prices for their shares drop considerably on Wednesday even as the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index climbed.
Tesla shares declined Wednesday afternoon and wiped out about $40 billion from the electric carmaker’s market capitalization, standing at $1.54 trillion. SpaceX also lost about $40 billion from its market value, now at $1.83 trillion.
Musk lost about $45 billion of his net worth on Wednesday, which stood at $865.6 billion, according to Forbes, though it could rebound.
Investors are signaling some jitters about the impact of the election on Musk’s businesses. Worries that he may face congressional investigations “contributed to the early plunge for his benchmark firms,” said Joe Mazzola, head trading and derivatives strategist at Charles Schwab.
Musk’s genius is also his danger, said Michael Morris, a professor of leadership at Columbia Business School.
“I can understand that the same strategic mind that makes him so good at some of the business ventures and the hedging, it makes him think that he can also take control of politics, but it’s a different animal,” he said.
“He obviously has way more money than he will ever need, and his companies are doing well,” Morris continued. “I do think it’s kind of a game to him.”
Musk now faces a leery Congress
Democrats have not forgotten Musk’s time in Washington last year heading DOGE, which blitzed through agencies culling federal workers, and a recent fiasco in which SpaceX internet service in Ukraine, Starlink, was throttled amid the war with Russia.
“Elon Musk waved a chain saw on stage and laughed while he fired public servants and gutted the services Americans rely on,” wrote Rep. James Walkinshaw, a Virginia Democrat, in an X post just before the election. “He must answer for it under oath.”
Back home in Texas, with an incoming Democratic governor, Musk’s dealings with the state, including tax breaks, could face similar scrutiny.
In August, Musk’s companies received a $30 million grant through a state program to build a semiconductor plant that is estimated to create 3,000 jobs, one of several cash infusions he’s received through state programs. And he’s successfully pushed the state legislature to pass laws favorable to his businesses.
Musk has also railed against what he’s called the “woke mind virus,” which appears to be a partisan motivation for him, and shot off a slew of posts on X leading up to the election against Talarico, almost entirely for past stances the Democrat has taken on transgender rights and other progressive causes. That was Paxton’s central attack against Talarico, too, though it fell far short.
“You know you couldn’t pull the wool over their eyes anymore with these culture wars, and they are frustrated with the costs,” said Rep. Christina Morales, a state Democrat from Houston now in the majority in the state’s House.
“We’re not saying you don’t belong here,” she said, but “Texans can’t be bought.”

title: 8 arrested in deadly block party mass shooting, 2 on the run
text:
DOOLY COUNTY, Ga. (WALB/Gray News) - More people have been charged in connection with a deadly Georgia mass shooting that left two people dead and 44 injured.
In a press conference on Thursday, Nov. 5, law enforcement officials announced that eight people were charged following multiple searches across Crisp, Dooly and Houston counties.
Those arrested on Nov. 5. include:
- Latravis Keonta Bentley, 19, of Vienna, Ga.
- Ty’Darrious Ty’Jai Dawson, age 19, of Cordele, Ga.
- Devontre Jaquon Holton, age 23, of Cordele, Ga.
- Demari Jaheem Nixon, age 23, of Cordele, Ga.
- Kahdarious Kayvon Ray, age 17, of Vienna, Ga.
- Keontae Towns, age 16, of Cordele, Ga.
However, two additional suspects identified as 19-year-old Brexton Esamuel Gaston of Cordele and 34-year-old Vanravious Rashad Williams of Perry have warrants out for their arrests and are considered “armed and dangerous,” Peavy said.
Each is facing a number of serious charges including felony murder, aggravated assault, aggravated battery, participation of street gang activity, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony and Possession of a firearm under the age of 21, according to the GBI.
Ray was also previously arrested on Oct. 9 but now faces additional charges, while two others were arrested in the case on Oct. 14.
Investigators say that several guns were recovered during the searches on Thursday, and determined that several automatic weapons, including rifles and handguns, were used in the homecoming block party mass shooting on Oct. 4.
Authorities added that a total of 28 people were shot, including Ja’Quavion Aderious Jackson and Macaleb Malik Jackson, who died from their injuries, while 16 others were injured while fleeing the scene.
The GBI says the investigation remains ongoing and anyone with information is urged to contact its Perry office at 478-987-4545 or submit an anonymous tip at 1-800-597-8477.

title: Animal rights group petitions Maine to adopt rules for salmon farms
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
An animal rights group has petitioned the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to establish new rules improving the welfare of farmed salmon in aquaculture operations.
Animal Outlook, a Washington-based animal welfare nonprofit, launched the petition drive. The group has previously campaigned against major agricultural brands, including poultry giant Tyson Foods, Nestlé, Dreyer’s and Häagen-Dazs.
The group submitted the petition under the Maine Administrative Procedure Act, which allows citizens to request that state agencies adopt or modify rules. State law requires the department to begin rulemaking proceedings within 60 days of receiving a petition signed by at least 150 registered Maine voters.
The process requires the department to review the petition and offer the public an opportunity to submit comments.
A department spokesperson said officials received the petition Sept. 29 and expect to begin the rulemaking process later this month.
Ben Williamson, Animal Outlook’s executive director, said the group took action after conducting two investigations into conditions at Cooke Aquaculture USA’s Bingham hatchery. In 2019, the group — then called Compassion Over Killing — released undercover video from the facility showing fungal infections and workers manhandling fish.
The department responded with an investigation, but Williamson said officials focused primarily on encouraging Cooke to voluntarily improve its practices.
Cooke Aquaculture USA, the U.S. subsidiary of Cooke Inc., holds 24 active permits covering 620 acres of Maine waters. With locations stretching from Swan’s Island and Frenchboro in the Midcoast north to Eastport, it is by far the state’s largest finfish aquaculture operation.
Parent company Cooke Inc., headquartered in New Brunswick, Canada, also manages 64 fish pen leases in Passamaquoddy Bay through Kelly Cove Salmon Ltd. The company sells its farmed salmon in the United States under the brand name True North.
Animal Outlook investigated the Bingham hatchery a second time late last year and found the same practices it documented in 2019 were ongoing.
Although this marks the second time Animal Outlook has criticized Cooke, Williamson said the organization targets industry practices rather than specific companies.
“We’re targeting finfish aquaculture the same way we go after poultry or pork producers, regardless of what company runs the facility,” he said.
In early 2019, True North Seafood announced a product collaboration with Martha Stewart, but she later dropped that collaboration. Following its latest investigation, Animal Outlook presented its findings to Hannaford, the Scarborough-based supermarket chain and primary distributor in Maine of True North products. Hannaford replied that it had received a 90-day corrective action plan from Cooke.
Last month, FarmStand, another Washington-based animal welfare organization, filed a consumer deception lawsuit in New York against Hannaford and its parent company, Ahold Delhaize USA. The lawsuit alleges the grocery chain deceptively markets its farm-raised seafood as sustainable.
Cooke Aquaculture USA also faces a lawsuit filed last year by the Conservation Law Foundation alleging the company violated the Clean Water Act. The lawsuit claims Cooke discharged uneaten fish food, feces, dead fish, chemicals and fuel into Maine waters.
The lawsuit describes “dead zones” around Cooke’s net pens, areas where trash from company sites prevents fishing, a “thick layer of toxic sediment on the ocean floor” and lobster traps covered in a “foul-smelling black sludge.”
Cooke sought to dismiss the lawsuit, but a U.S. District Court judge in Maine ruled in September that the case could proceed, as reported by Inside Climate News.
Cooke Aquaculture USA did not respond to a request for comment.
This story appears as part of a collaboration to strengthen investigative journalism in Maine between the BDN and The Maine Monitor. Read more about the partnership.

title: Obituary: William E. “Bill” Gilpatric
text:
KENNEBUNK – William E. “Bill” Gilpatric passed away on Nov. 2, 2026, surrounded by his loving family. Born on Dec. 21, 1937, Bill shared 60 years of marriage with his wife, Sally, and a life filled with love for his family, dedication to his community, and enjoyment of Maine’s outdoors. He dearly loved his children and grandchildren and took great pride in watching them grow into the people they are today. A true Mainer through and through, Bill had a wonderful sense of humor and loved a good joke.
Bill graduated from Thornton Academy with the Class of 1956. He loved football and played on Thornton Academy’s state championship teams in 1954 and 1955. He attended Iowa State College on a full football scholarship before returning to Maine and graduating from Northeastern Business College with a degree in accounting and business administration.
Bill began his career at W.L. Blake and Company in Portland before joining Kennebunk Savings Bank, where he spent 31 years, including 18 years as president.
After retiring from Kennebunk Savings Bank, Bill joined Advest, Inc. as a financial advisor in September 1993. His daughter, Susan, joined him in the business, and they worked side by side for 10 years. Bill later retired from Wachovia Securities in 2009.
Service was an important part of Bill’s life. He served in the Maine Air National Guard from 1961 to 1967 and was a 64-year member of Saco Lodge #9 F. & A.M. He was also a lifetime member of the Sportsman’s Alliance of Maine.
Throughout his life, Bill gave generously of his time to his community. He served as a director, treasurer, and president of the York County Fish & Game Association and as a director of the Northern York County YMCA and United Way. He also served on the boards of York County Technical College and Huntington Common. He was president of the Webhannet Golf Club and a member and past president of the Kennebunk Rotary Club, where he was recognized as a Paul Harris Fellow. He was also a member of the Arundel Yacht Club.
Bill also served as Finance Committee chairman and a Cabinet member at Christ Church, a director of the Brick Store Museum, and treasurer and director of Ducks Unlimited.
His commitment to service extended to the banking and insurance communities. Bill was a director of Blue Cross Blue Shield of Maine; chairman and trustee of the Maine Financial Institutions Insurance Trust; and an Executive Committee member of the Maine Association of Community Banks. He also served as chairman and director of the Savings Banks Association of Maine, director and Executive Committee member of the National Association of Community Banks, and director of Community and Savings Bankers of America.
An avid outdoorsman, Bill enjoyed every Maine season and loved spending time at his camp on Douglas Mountain. He loved hunting, fishing, snowmobiling, and spending time aboard his boat, Sea Alice. He also enjoyed golf, tying flies, and working in his garden, and he took up downhill skiing at the age of 50. In retirement, he enjoyed spending winters at The Villages in Florida.
He was predeceased by his parents, Ruannah and Charlie Gilpatric; and his brother, Jeff Gilpatric.
Bill leaves his beloved wife, Sally; their two children, Susan Gilpatric (John Smart) and Jason Gilpatric (Heidi); and his three cherished grandchildren, Abigail Gilpatric, William “Liam” Gilpatric, and Ryan Smart.
Bill’s family extends heartfelt thanks to the Care Partners at The Mooring of Kennebunk and the staff at Affinity Hospice for their kind and compassionate care.
A private family burial will be held. A celebration of Bill’s life will be held on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. at Webhannet Golf Club, 26 Golf Club Drive, Kennebunk.
To share a memory or leave a message of condolence, please visit Bill’s Book of Memories Page at http://www.bibberfuneral.com.
Arrangements are in care of Bibber Memorial Chapel, 67 Summer St., Kennebunk, ME 04043.

title: Local cross country teams win championships this fall
text:
WINTHROP, HAMPDEN, BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - The Winthrop Ramblers won the Class C state boys cross country championship on Saturday at Cony High School.
The victory is sweet for the Ramblers after they finished as runners-up last season.
“We had to just try to survive on that uphill because that was a mean uphill. But then after that, it was flat. We had to groove that whole downhill. That was a big point in that race where it was like, we got it,” said Alfie Cognata, senior.
“It means a lot to me to get my high school career going with the state championship. It means a lot,” said Sawyer Wess, freshman.
“It feels great. It’s been a long four years, a lot of training. It’s nice to end my senior year winning states,” said Sam St. Germain, senior.
The Hampden Academy Broncos captured the Class A state girls cross country title.
They spoke about winning it all after last year’s third-place finish.
“I’m really grateful for my team. I’m really happy we all got to do it together. This has been something we’ve been wanting for the past few years. For it to happen my senior year, it’s really special to me,” said Isabelle Clark, senior.
“We really focused on positivity and being connected as a team. We stayed humble, and we work really well together and push each other,” said Addison Elliott, senior.
“We’re a really good hill running team. I think just having Cony as a really hilly race, that’s really good for us,” said Mackenzie Elliott, freshman.
“It just felt really good to have all of our training pay off and be able to celebrate together,” said Sylvia Ruge, sophomore.
Winthrop and Hampden are preparing to run in the New England Championship on Saturday of next weekend at Belfast’s Troy Howard Middle School.
The Husson Eagles won the NAC women’s cross country championship with five runners in the top-10 finishers.
Saturday’s title at UMaine Farmington is the fifth conference crown in team history.
“It feels really good. We’ve worked really hard this season. It’s been a season of grit and perseverance, and we really all did it together,” said Lucinda Carroll, junior.
“It was the very start. We knew we could do it, and we kind of had that mentality the whole season. We knew we were prepared for it, and we did everything we could to make us stronger and ready for it,” said Elise Ouellette, freshman.
Next up for the Eagles is the NCAA Division III East Regional Championship on Saturday of next weekend at South Portland’s Wainwright Recreation Complex.
